newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UM still a 'buy' despite SGB sale.
newsitem.headline: UM still a 'buy' despite SGB sale.

text.p: Shares in Belgian non-ferrous metals company Union Miniere are still a 'buy' despite the sale by its main shareholder, holding company Societe Generale de Belgique (SGB) of about half its stake.

Analysts said prospects for Union Miniere, widely seen as a turnaround stock, were good and predicted further support from relatively high prices for zinc -- of which UM is a major producer -- and a strong dollar.

They also said that the fact that Societe Generale, via a bank consortium, re-placed shares at prices of around 3,400 francs -- below a record 3,795 franc high set on July 7 -- was an indication of scope for further gains.

A major broker such as Merrill Lynch, reportedly leading the consortium, would not be selling the shares at around those levels if it did not think the operation would succeed and if it did not think there was upside potential, analysts said.
Union Miniere was down 295 francs at 3,450 at Wednesday's bourse close, continuing a correction from the July 7 high.
Dealers said Wednesday's fall was the result of some investors instantly selling part of the shares they had obtained in the re-placement on the market.

Over the past two days Union Miniere lost some nine percent, exceeding the five to seven percent corrections seen earlier this year and signalling that heavier than usual selling was going on, analysts said.
They said the share should at the latest find support in the 3,200 - 3,285 franc area, marking its break out of the recent trend channel at the end of last month.
"At current levels the share can be bought," analyst Patrick Millecam at brokerage Corluy & Co said. "Union Miniere is a good stock," Luc Vander Elst at Generale Bank said.

Analysts predicted a sharp recovery in company results this year and next. Earnings per share (EPS) are forecast to shoot up to 155/166 francs in 1997 and rise further to 221/234 francs in 1998. EPS was 65 francs in 1996.

Some analysts, however, said the wide range of forecasts -- 103 to 244 francs for 1997 and 154 to 335 francs for 1998 -- signalled not all analysts were equally convinced about the strength of the cyclical company's recovery.
Union Miniere itself said in May it expected results for this year to better than those of 1996 when it returned to profit for the first time in five years.
Analysts have said 1997 should see the first contributions to results of a streamlining and cost-cutting restructuring plan which Union Miniere put in operation in 1995.

Societe Generale said on Wednesday it sold a 24 percent stake in Union Miniere. It would be using the revenue of about 20 billion francs ($550.8 million), including a capital gain of about 12 billion francs, to help cut debt.
In the wake of the news Societe Generale shares lost 80 francs to close at 3,650 francs as the market adjusted its price for the loss of about half its holding in Union Miniere.
"The surplus value from Union Miniere which you as an investor thought you had yesterday by holding Societe Generale is gone today," one analyst said, explaining the share price correction.
